speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Six, and you are on the stones. I said I would not hold a string for a farewell.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The farewell is on the other side of the door. She has had it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Light this time, and no calls at Oxford. Four days. Eight when I'm laden and the way's foul.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four. The horses may hear it as well. I have heard it once, and that is enough.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Gloves, cheeses, and a town's letters under the cloths. A bell on the leader, so the string knows which end of itself is the front.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Richard has put the parcel up.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: He handed it up and made no speech of the knot. Leave him that. A brother who can be silent at a bridge is a useful brother.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Don't praise him where he can decide to answer. He said last night he would not be helped, and he has kept it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Up. The spare, from here to Shipston. Ten miles. You carry nothing. You sit like a sack, and the sack is an order, not an insult.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I can walk the first mile.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: You can walk it into the ditch I named you yesterday. The back rides. After Shipston you may be proud on your own feet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not glad of it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Say so. The nag does not keep a tally of what a man is glad of. Two and a half miles in the hour, up or down, because I will not keep one pace for a proud man and another for a horse.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No calls. I am not a post, and you are not a post.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Oxford has too many tongues already. I will not add yours to a tavern. A man who wants you can want you in London, where wanting you is his own affair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The two shillings is at the Bell. Not on this bridge. My mother is not in this yard.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: The Bell. I have it in my head with the cheeses. If you pay me in a kitchen I have to explain a kitchen, and I am a carrier, not a clerk of kitchens.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Past the rise, the old stones are on the right. I am not turning aside for them.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Long Compton is a rise, not a shrine. You walk it when you are off this nag. You do not improve the road by looking at it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then put me up. I will hate the ten miles, and you may tell the horses I said so.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: They have heard worse from a barrel of nails. Hold the mane. Leave the speech. We go when the bell says we go.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bell is yours. The not-glad is mine. I can carry both as far as Shipston, so long as I carry nothing else.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Nothing else. Not a horn, not a quarrel, not a house. Four days. If the clay is up it will be eight, and you will hear it from me before you hear it from a mile.
